title: SAVE: Software-Implemented Fault Tolerance for Model Inference against GPU Memory Bit Flips
problem: GPU memory bit flips can silently corrupt model weights and activations during inference, causing incorrect predictions. Software-based protection mechanisms are needed that don't require hardware ECC or full model replication.
motivation: GPU-based deep learning inference is widely deployed in production systems, and transient memory faults pose an increasing reliability risk as memory densities grow.
method: SAVE implements software-based fault tolerance for GPU model inference through detection and recovery mechanisms applied at the software level. The approach likely uses redundancy, error detection codes, or selective re-execution to identify and mitigate the effects of memory bit flips without requiring hardware modifications.
key_novelty: Software-only fault tolerance approach for GPU model inference that protects against memory bit flips without hardware ECC or memory duplication.
contributions: Software fault tolerance framework for GPU model inference
Mechanism for detecting memory bit flips in GPU computations
Efficient recovery strategy with manageable performance overhead
limitations: Not discussed; analysis limited to title only without abstract or full paper access.
primary_theme: software-based GPU fault tolerance for inference
